eq.title: How ptr::eq works
eq.description: true if two references point to the same place in memory.

slides.caption: b has the same value but lives elsewhere: false.
Rc::ptr_eq does the same for Rc pointers.

null.title: How ptr::null works
null.description: A raw pointer that points nowhere.

slides.caption: Safe Rust uses Option instead; null pointers appear when talking to C.
Creating one is safe; reading through it is undefined behaviour.

null_mut.title: How ptr::null_mut works
null_mut.description: A mutable raw pointer that points nowhere.

slides.caption: Safe Rust uses Option instead of null.
Writing through it is undefined behaviour.

addr_eq.title: How ptr::addr_eq works
addr_eq.description: Compares only the addresses of two pointers, ignoring extra metadata.

slides.caption: A slice pointer carries a length; addr_eq ignores it.
Both start at the same address.
ptr::eq would also compare the metadata.

slice_from_raw_parts.title: How ptr::slice_from_raw_parts works
slice_from_raw_parts.description: Builds a raw slice pointer from a start pointer and a length.

slides.caption: Creating it is safe; reading through it is not.

without_provenance.title: How ptr::without_provenance works
without_provenance.description: A pointer with a given address that may not be used to access memory.

slides.caption: Useful for tagged or sentinel pointers that are never dereferenced.

is_null.title: How <*const T>::is_null works
is_null.description: true if the raw pointer is null.

slides.caption: Pointers from C may be null.
as_ref (unsafe) turns a pointer into Option<&T>.

cast.title: How <*const T>::cast works
cast.description: Changes the pointee type of a raw pointer.

slides.caption: Safer than as, because only the pointee type changes.
Reading through the new type is still unsafe.

addr.title: How <*const T>::addr works
addr.description: The address of a pointer as a usize.

slides.caption: Neighbouring i32 elements are 4 bytes apart.
Do not turn the usize back into a pointer with as.

wrapping_add.title: How <*const T>::wrapping_add works
wrapping_add.description: Moves a raw pointer by n elements, without unsafe.

slides.caption: The arithmetic is safe; reading the result is unsafe.
add (unsafe) promises to stay inside the allocation.

new.title: How NonNull::new works
new.description: Wraps a raw pointer that is guaranteed not to be null; None if it is.

slides.caption: Option<NonNull<T>> is the same size as a raw pointer.
Used to build linked lists and other raw structures.

dangling.title: How NonNull::dangling works
dangling.description: A non-null, well-aligned pointer that must not be read.

slides.caption: Vec uses it for an empty buffer that has no allocation.

as_ptr.title: How NonNull::as_ptr works
as_ptr.description: The raw *mut T inside a NonNull.

slides.caption: Use it to read or write through unsafe code.

from_ref.title: How NonNull::from_ref works
from_ref.description: A NonNull from a shared reference (references are never null).

slides.caption: No check needed: references cannot be null.
The type itself says the address is not 0.
Useful for hashing or tagging pointers.

add.title: How <*const T>::add works
add.description: Moves a pointer forward by n elements (unsafe: must stay inside the allocation).

slides.caption: n counts elements, not bytes: add(2) on *const i32 moves 8 bytes.
wrapping_add is the safe version that may leave the allocation.

sub.title: How <*const T>::sub works
sub.description: Moves a pointer backward by n elements (unsafe).

slides.caption: Must stay within the same allocation.
Pointing one past the end is allowed; reading there is not.

offset.title: How <*const T>::offset works
offset.description: Moves a pointer by a signed number of elements (unsafe).

slides.caption: offset accepts negative values; add/sub take usize.
add and sub read better when the direction is known.

offset_from.title: How <*const T>::offset_from works
offset_from.description: How many elements apart two pointers into the same allocation are (signed, unsafe).

slides.caption: Both pointers must point into the same allocation.
q is three elements after p.
offset_from_unsigned returns a usize when the order is known.

offset_from_unsigned.title: How <*const T>::offset_from_unsigned works
offset_from_unsigned.description: The element distance from an earlier pointer, as a usize (unsafe).

note.text: q must not be before p

slides.caption: Undefined behaviour if q is before p.

byte_add.title: How <*const T>::byte_add works
byte_add.description: Moves a pointer forward by n bytes, keeping its type (unsafe).

slides.caption: add(1) does the same for i32.

byte_sub.title: How <*const T>::byte_sub works
byte_sub.description: Moves a pointer backward by n bytes (unsafe).

slides.caption: The result must be properly aligned before reading.

byte_offset.title: How <*const T>::byte_offset works
byte_offset.description: Moves a pointer by a signed number of bytes (unsafe).

byte_offset_from.title: How <*const T>::byte_offset_from works
byte_offset_from.description: How many bytes apart two pointers are (signed, unsafe).

slides.caption: The pointers may have different types.

byte_offset_from_unsigned.title: How <*const T>::byte_offset_from_unsigned works
byte_offset_from_unsigned.description: The byte distance from an earlier pointer, as a usize (unsafe).

slides.caption: Undefined if q is before p.

wrapping_offset.title: How <*const T>::wrapping_offset works
wrapping_offset.description: Moves a pointer by a signed element count; safe, but the result may not be readable.

slides.caption: Computing it is safe; reading is only valid inside the allocation.
offset (unsafe) promises to stay in bounds, which helps optimisation.

wrapping_sub.title: How <*const T>::wrapping_sub works
wrapping_sub.description: Moves a pointer back by n elements; safe to compute.

slides.caption: May leave the allocation without undefined behaviour.
sub is the unsafe, in-bounds version.

wrapping_byte_add.title: How <*const T>::wrapping_byte_add works
wrapping_byte_add.description: Moves a pointer forward by n bytes; safe to compute.

slides.caption: Reading still needs alignment and bounds.
byte_add is the unsafe, in-bounds version.

wrapping_byte_sub.title: How <*const T>::wrapping_byte_sub works
wrapping_byte_sub.description: Moves a pointer backward by n bytes; safe to compute.

slides.caption: The pointer type does not change.

wrapping_byte_offset.title: How <*const T>::wrapping_byte_offset works
wrapping_byte_offset.description: Moves a pointer by a signed number of bytes; safe to compute.

read.title: How <*const T>::read works
read.description: Copies the value out of the pointer, without moving it out of the source (unsafe).

read_unaligned.title: How <*const T>::read_unaligned works
read_unaligned.description: Reads a value from an address that may not be properly aligned (unsafe).

slides.caption: Normal reads require alignment; this one does not.

Common when parsing packed binary formats.

read_volatile.title: How <*const T>::read_volatile works
read_volatile.description: A read the compiler must not remove or merge (unsafe).

slides.caption: The compiler keeps every volatile access exactly as written.
Not a synchronisation tool between threads; use atomics for that.

copy_to.title: How <*const T>::copy_to works
copy_to.description: Copies n elements from this pointer to another; the regions may overlap (unsafe).

copy_to_nonoverlapping.title: How <*const T>::copy_to_nonoverlapping works
copy_to_nonoverlapping.description: Copies n elements to a region that must not overlap (unsafe).

as_ref.title: How <*const T>::as_ref works
as_ref.description: Turns a raw pointer into Option<&T>: None for null (unsafe).

slides.caption: You promise the pointer is valid if it is not null.

as_ref_unchecked.title: How <*const T>::as_ref_unchecked works
as_ref_unchecked.description: Turns a raw pointer into &T without a null check (unsafe).

slides.caption: Faster when you already know it is valid.

cast_mut.title: How <*const T>::cast_mut works
cast_mut.description: Changes *const T into *mut T, keeping the address.

slides.caption: Writing through it is only allowed if the memory is really mutable.

is_aligned.title: How <*const T>::is_aligned works
is_aligned.description: true if the address is a multiple of the type's alignment.

slides.caption: Misaligned reads are undefined behaviour (use read_unaligned).

align_offset tells how far to the next aligned address.

align_offset.title: How <*const T>::align_offset works
align_offset.description: How many elements to move to reach the next address aligned to a value.

a0t.text: *const u8 at offset 1 of a u32 buffer

slides.caption: ...3 bytes to the next multiple of 4.

expose_provenance.title: How <*const T>::expose_provenance works
expose_provenance.description: The address as a usize, allowing it to be turned back into a pointer later.

slides.caption: with_exposed_provenance turns the number back into a usable pointer.
Prefer addr() when you never need the pointer back.

with_addr.title: How <*const T>::with_addr works
with_addr.description: A pointer with a new address but the same provenance (permission to access).

slides.caption: The new address must stay inside the original allocation to be readable.
map_addr applies a function to the address.

map_addr.title: How <*const T>::map_addr works
map_addr.description: Changes a pointer's address with a function, keeping its provenance.

slides.caption: Used to store flags in the low bits of aligned pointers.
Clear any tag bits before dereferencing.

len.title: How <*const [T]>::len works
len.description: The length of a raw slice pointer, read from its metadata.

slides.caption: A slice pointer carries its length alongside the address.
Safe: it never reads the elements.

is_empty.title: How <*const [T]>::is_empty works
is_empty.description: true if a raw slice pointer has length 0.

as_array.title: How <*const [T]>::as_array works
as_array.description: Turns a slice pointer into an array pointer if the length matches exactly.

mut_ptr-offset_from_unsigned.description: The element distance from an earlier pointer as usize (unsafe).

mut_ptr-byte_offset.title: How <*mut T>::byte_offset works

mut_ptr-byte_offset_from.description: The signed byte distance between two pointers (unsafe).

mut_ptr-byte_offset_from_unsigned.title: How <*mut T>::byte_offset_from_unsigned works
mut_ptr-byte_offset_from_unsigned.description: The byte distance from an earlier pointer as usize (unsafe).

slides.caption: q must not be before p.

mut_ptr-wrapping_add.title: How <*mut T>::wrapping_add works
mut_ptr-wrapping_add.description: Moves forward by n elements; safe to compute.

slides.caption: Writing still requires a valid location.

mut_ptr-wrapping_sub.title: How <*mut T>::wrapping_sub works
mut_ptr-wrapping_sub.description: Moves back by n elements; safe to compute.

mut_ptr-wrapping_offset.title: How <*mut T>::wrapping_offset works
mut_ptr-wrapping_offset.description: Moves by a signed element count; safe to compute.

mut_ptr-wrapping_byte_add.title: How <*mut T>::wrapping_byte_add works
mut_ptr-wrapping_byte_add.description: Moves forward by n bytes; safe to compute.

mut_ptr-wrapping_byte_sub.title: How <*mut T>::wrapping_byte_sub works
mut_ptr-wrapping_byte_sub.description: Moves back by n bytes; safe to compute.

mut_ptr-wrapping_byte_offset.title: How <*mut T>::wrapping_byte_offset works
mut_ptr-wrapping_byte_offset.description: Moves by a signed number of bytes; safe to compute.

mut_ptr-read.description: Copies the value out of a mutable pointer (unsafe).

mut_ptr-read_unaligned.title: How <*mut T>::read_unaligned works
mut_ptr-read_unaligned.description: Reads from a possibly misaligned address (unsafe).

mut_ptr-read_volatile.description: A read the compiler must keep exactly as written (unsafe).

write_bytes.title: How <*mut T>::write_bytes works

mut_ptr-copy_to_nonoverlapping.description: Copies n elements to a separate region (unsafe).

hash.title: How ptr::hash works
hash.description: Hashes a pointer's address (not the value it points to).

slides.caption: Useful for hash sets of objects by identity.
Hashing *p would hash the value instead.

fn_addr_eq.title: How ptr::fn_addr_eq works
fn_addr_eq.description: Compares two function pointers by address.

slides.caption: Function addresses are not always unique: the compiler may merge or duplicate them.
Do not rely on different functions having different addresses.

slice_from_raw_parts_mut.title: How ptr::slice_from_raw_parts_mut works
slice_from_raw_parts_mut.description: Builds a *mut [T] from a start pointer and a length.

ptr-with_exposed_provenance.title: How ptr::with_exposed_provenance works
ptr-with_exposed_provenance.description: Turns an exposed address back into a *const T.

slides.caption: Only for addresses that were exposed.

with_exposed_provenance_mut.title: How ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut works
with_exposed_provenance_mut.description: Turns an exposed address back into a *mut T.

slides.caption: Used in FFI with integer handles.

without_provenance_mut.title: How ptr::without_provenance_mut works
without_provenance_mut.description: A *mut T with an address but no permission to access memory.
